A partial 3333 of a 11000 basket containing a discount line allocated to full_price=3030, discount=-454, physical_goods=757, summing exactly to 3333, with checkAllocation running BEFORE the insert; a second collection on the same request moved partially_paid then paid correctly. Reasoned, not just executed: a component cannot silently go missing, because one row is emitted per frozen line and checkAllocation refuses the set unless the gross components sum to what Stripe collected. (6) THE BACKWARD-WALK GUARD ON THE SETTLE PATH HOLDS. With the request at `refunded` and at `partially_refunded`, a redelivered succeeded returned already_settled / statusMovedTo null and changed nothing. | no |

Cart rows store POINTERS ONLY (no price, no title), so stale pricing is eliminated by construction rather than by cache invalidation. The cart feeds the EXISTING checkout core through one additive nullable cartId thread - no parallel money path, no client-submitted selections, and therefore no new fee arithmetic (inherited whole). | Mobile JSON API routes and web server actions: authentication, ownership scoping, input validation, error handling, IDOR and cache revalidation / authz | substantial | SCOPE AS ASSIGNED, all read in full: 17 mobile route files (booking-form + fields + fields/[id] + confirmation, goods + [id] + [id]/status + collections + discounts, projects + [id], settings/appearance + email-templates + hub + slug, travel/studios + travel/trips) and 18 server-action files ((artist) bookings/booking-form, bookings/form, bookings/books, bookings/projects, bookings/settings, goods, goods/collections, goods/discounts, settings/appearance, settings/books, settings/plan, settings/profile/slug-actions, studio; plus [slug], [slug]/project, request/[token], legal/report, (map)/map). Because most actions are thin wrappers, the shared cores they delegate to were read too and are the substantive part of the coverage: lib/server/mobile-auth.ts, collections.ts, discount-write.ts, projects.ts, goods-variants.ts, slug-rename.ts, appearance-write.ts, confirmation-write.ts, map-watch.ts, plus lib/ratelimit.ts, lib/image-guard.ts, lib/image-processing.ts and lib/mobile-goods.ts. LIMB 1, AUTHENTICATION — CLEAN, no exceptions. All 17 mobile routes begin with `requireMobileUser(req)` and return before touching data on failure. All 18 action files resolve the user through the cookie client and refuse when absent. requireMobileUser itself (mobile-auth.ts:28-75) validates the bearer token via supabase.auth.getUser, builds an RLS-SCOPED anon-key client rather than a service client, and adds a suspension gate that deliberately fails OPEN on a missing profile with the reasoning stated in the file. The one unauthenticated action in scope, submitProjectIntakeAction, is unauthenticated by design (it is a public intake) and is covered by ABUSE-PUB-001 for what it lacks INSTEAD of auth, not for lacking auth. LIMB 2, OWNERSHIP AND IDOR — CLEAN. I looked specifically for an id taken from the URL or body and used without an owner predicate, and did not find one in the assigned scope. Every write carries `.eq("artist_id", userId)` (or `.eq("id", userId)` on profiles) in the same statement, not in a preceding read. The service-role uses are the interesting cases and each one was traced: projects.ts runs service-role because RLS 0115 gives the artist SELECT only, and every one of loadProject / setProjectStatusCore / saveProjectNoteCore / linkBookingToProjectCore carries `.eq("artist_id", artistId)` with a rowcount check; booking-form/fields/[id] DELETE uses the service client solely to COUNT booking_requests, and scopes that count to the artist; goods-variants.ts reconcileVariants runs service-role but scopes every update and delete to `.eq("product_id", productId)` after the caller has ownership-checked the product with an RLS read. Three positive defences worth recording because they are easy to get wrong and are right here: goods/actions.ts:326-327 refuses a keep-list image URL that is not already on the product, which blocks a cross-artist graft or delete; travel/studios POST deliberately does not accept the Google Places columns from the body so a crafted request cannot inject a google_maps_url onto a public block; and request/[token] prepareCheckoutAction allowlists every add-on against the artist-confirmed booking_interests rows and caps quantity at what the artist vouched for. LIMB 3, INPUT VALIDATION — sound, with the shape stated. No route uses `await request.json()` output directly in a query. Bodies go through a named validator (normalizeProductInput, normalizeStudioInput, normalizeTripInput, normalizeFieldInput + the shared zod fieldConfigSchema, parseBioPageSettings, parseAppearance, parseConfirmationPage) or through a core that validates. Where coercion is lenient it is deliberate and commented (unrecognised category/status/currency fall back to a safe default, matching the web action). Two fail-closed choices were checked and hold: mobile-goods.ts:103 publishes only on an explicit boolean true, and settings/hub POST refuses a non-object body rather than letting the parser treat it as DEFAULT_BIO_PAGE and wipe the config. UUID_RE guards the path parameter on projects/[id] and booking-form/fields/[id]. LIMB 4, ERROR HANDLING — one finding, OPS-ERR-001. Every route wraps req.json() in try/catch and returns a fixed 400. LIMB 5, ERROR-HANDLING CONSISTENCY — the sibling comparison found real but minor divergence, recorded here rather than as a finding because nothing is unsafe: goods/[id] PUT and goods/[id]/status PATCH both do an explicit existence read and return a structured 404, while booking-form/fields/[id] PATCH does not, so a PATCH naming a non-existent or foreign field id matches zero rows, produces no error and returns 200 {ok:true}. The DELETE verb in that same file DOES return 404. Similarly, mobile goods/discounts PATCH maps every setDiscountActiveCore failure to 500, including the "That code no longer exists." case which is a 404. Neither leaks data or permits a write. LIMB 6, REVALIDATION — one finding, BILL-UI-001, and it is the only mutation in the audited set without one. Counted the other way: 8 collections actions, 2 discounts, 7 goods, 18 studio, 5 bookings/settings, books, appearance, slug (layout-wide), projects, map, and the mobile hub route (which revalidates the PUBLIC /<slug>/hub) all revalidate. | no |
